title: Isolated Downstream Validation and Single‑Repair Effects in Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study cand-003-stud-001) that isolates purely downstream deterministic validation plus a bounded single-repair intervention under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using 1,000 deterministic intents (1,000 paired episodes) drawn from a synthetic workflow stress corpus and a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; any paired outcome difference can therefore arise only from the validator decision and at most one permitted repair call (guarded arm). Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; discordants n10 = 5 (guarded only), n01 = 0 (baseline only); preregistered primary test exact two‑sided McNemar p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). Preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.001, 0.01]. Total hosted model calls recorded = 1005 (1000 shared initial + 5 repair). We present the exact McNemar as the confirmatory inference, the bootstrap interval as a preregistered descriptive summary, and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, ceiling effects, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating translation from operator intent to device configuration promises operational efficiency but raises safety risks: incorrect command ordering, transient invariant violations, and unauthorized touches of protected fields can convert plausible plans into damaging live changes. Empirical surveys and benchmarks document hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that reduce correctness in code- and config-like generation and motivate verifier‑augmented architectures that detect and sometimes repair unsafe outputs [1],[2].

This paper reports a preregistered paired experiment explicitly designed to isolate the marginal effect of a deterministic validator and a bounded single-repair invocation when both experimental arms reuse the exact same initial sampled candidate (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate). Our estimand is the paired success‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) on complete pairs. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics no first‑pass sampling difference exists between arms; therefore any paired outcome difference can only arise from the deterministic validator decision and the allowed at‑most‑one repair call. This causal framing differs from generate→validate→repair evaluations that mix validator effects with independent sampling or decoding changes and yields the precise estimand: baseline single‑shot/initial validity versus final guarded‑pipeline validity after deterministic validation and permitted repair.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired confirmatory study (Npairs = 1,000) using a challenging synthetic NetOps workflow stress corpus and archived validator traces. (2) Full execution accounting and explicit runtime configuration reporting, including the recorded model_configuration temperature = null/unset (we emphasize null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). (3) Transparent reporting of the preregistered primary inference (exact two‑sided McNemar, p = 0.0625), the preregistered paired bootstrap descriptive summary (95% percentile CI = [0.001, 0.01], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), and an evidence‑grounded interpretation that accounts for sparse discordants, near‑unity baseline, and validator scope.
sections.related_work:
Three strands of prior work motivate and contextualize our design. First, evaluation studies and surveys show that LLMs produce both syntactic and substantive errors in structured-output tasks (code, configs) and are sensitive to prompt and decoding choices; these failures materially affect downstream correctness and motivate verifier‑centric pipelines [3],[4]. Second, a body of systems and benchmark work proposes and demonstrates architectures that pair generation with validation and repair (generate→validate→repair); reported gains depend strongly on validator coverage, repair budgets, and benchmark construction [5],[6],[7]. Importantly, the literature warns that measured improvements conflate validator/repair efficacy with generator changes when sampling or prompt templates differ between compared conditions, so isolating downstream validator effects is a necessary step to unambiguously quantify validator marginal returns [5],[7]. Third, architecture and governance papers emphasize that operational reliability of agentic NetOps depends on protocol enforcement, auditability, and bounded tool interfaces (proof‑carrying traces, canaries, rollback policies); these works provide prototypes and design guidance but leave production-scale validation open [8],[9].

Two methodological lessons from this prior literature shaped our preregistered shared_initial_candidate design. (a) When comparisons allow independent first‑pass sampling across arms, attributing improvement to downstream validation alone is ambiguous; a shared‑candidate paired design eliminates this confound and isolates validator/repair marginal effects. (b) Constrained‑decoding or schema‑aware approaches can increase executable outputs in other structured domains (e.g., cheminformatics), but evidence typically relies on domain tooling and may not transfer directly to multi‑device NetOps where ordering and protected‑field policies dominate [11],[12]. Our study complements these results by fixing generation and measuring only deterministic downstream validation plus a single allowed repair.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. The study preregistration (cand-003-stud-001) was frozen prior to any hosted-model invocation. Core preregistered items executed without deviation include: task_count = 1,000 complete pairs; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused by both arms); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary confirmatory test = exact two‑sided McNemar. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI used 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729 as a descriptive summary.

Task corpus and deterministic selection. Tasks derive from a synthetic challenging_workflow_stress_v1 corpus. Selection deterministically maps ordinal j∈[0,999] to fixed task indices to yield 1,000 unique intents. Each manifest includes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty annotations (levels include 'very_hard' and 'extreme'). Typical workflows encode multi‑step operations with transient invariants (examples: failover_then_offline_reconfiguration, rolling_access_vlan_migration, safe_access_service_transfer, composed_redundancy_and_access_maintenance).

Adapter, declared model, and validator. The adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and the declared provider/model was gpt‑5‑mini. The recorded model_configuration shows temperature = null/unset; per preregistration we explicitly note null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms (shared_initial_candidate semantics); the guarded arm applies deterministic validator checks and may invoke at most one repair call if the validator rejects the initial candidate. The validator, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, is a deterministic digital‑twin emulator that parses candidate command sequences, enforces required command presence/order, protected‑field noninterference, and workflow invariants, and emits a binary safe‑deploy decision plus structured validation_before/after traces.

Causal semantics and analysis. Because baseline and guarded episodes for each pair share the identical initial candidate, any paired outcome difference can only arise from the deterministic validator decision and at most one permitted repair invocation. The preregistration explicitly set independent_condition_generation = false; no independent first‑pass generations were executed for alternate prompt or decoding arms, so generator‑level interventions are outside this estimand. The registered executor computed the exact two‑sided McNemar p‑value as the preregistered confirmatory test and a paired bootstrap percentile CI as a descriptive summary (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Bootstrap CIs are reported as prespecified descriptive quantities and do not replace the preregistered confirmatory decision rule.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. Planned episodes = 2,000; completed = 2,000; complete_pairs = 1,000; failed episodes = 0. Provider call audit recorded hosted model call event count = 1,005 (1,000 shared initial generations + 5 repair calls). The paired contingency table observed: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar yields p = 0.0625 (primary confirmatory inference; not < 0.05).

Preregistered bootstrap summary. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) computed by the registered executor is [0.001, 0.01]. The bootstrap CI is a prespecified descriptive summary; in this run the interval excludes zero despite the confirmatory p‑value being >0.05. This pattern reflects the discrete null distribution of McNemar tests when discordant counts are extremely sparse: bootstrap percentile bounds can omit zero while exact two‑sided tests remain nondiscovering because the discrete null concentrates mass on symmetric small counts.

Repair mechanics and diagnostics. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred. Archived validator traces for repaired pairs indicate the validator rejected the shared initial candidate for rule‑level violations (representative diagnostics include required_sequence ordering errors and unauthorized touches of protected interfaces), invoked a single repair call that produced a repaired candidate, and then revalidated that repaired candidate as acceptable. The repaired episodes are concentrated among higher‑difficulty patterns annotated 'very_hard' or 'extreme' and involve multi‑step required_sequences; total hosted model calls recorded = 1,005 and all deterministic reconciliation checks passed.

Representative artifacts. Representative per‑task artifacts (shared initial responses, baseline and guarded scoring outputs, and validator traces) are archived and document that every pair reused the same shared_initial_candidate and that validation_before and validation_after fields capture rule checks and repair_applied flags for guarded episodes.
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory vs descriptive evidence. By the preregistered decision rule the exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625) is the confirmatory outcome and does not reach two‑sided α = 0.05; we therefore do not claim confirmatory support for a nonzero paired increase under the prespecified two‑sided test. The paired bootstrap CI ([0.001, 0.01]) is a prespecified descriptive summary and aids interpretation; it does not override the preregistered confirmatory conclusion. A post‑hoc one‑sided McNemar (exploratory) gave p = 0.03125 and is explicitly labeled exploratory in the archived artifacts.

Statistical interpretation given sparse discordants and ceiling effects. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline≈0.60 and targeted an absolute increase of 0.15. Observed baseline = 0.995 is far higher than assumed; this concentrates mass in the concordant success cell (n11 = 995) and leaves only five discordant pairs. With n10 = 5 and n01 = 0 the exact two‑sided p = 0.0625 sits marginally above 0.05. Practically, when baseline validity is near unity, detecting tiny absolute gains (here 0.005) requires either much larger paired sample sizes or designs that increase discordant prevalence (e.g., independent generation arms, injected failures, or larger repair budgets). The bootstrap CI reflects sample‑level variability but—given the small discordant count—should be interpreted cautiously.

Failure‑mode diagnostics and scope of inference. Archived validator traces show the five repaired cases shared rule‑level failure modes: ordering violations in required_sequence and unauthorized touches of protected interfaces. These repaired tasks come from complex multi‑step workflows (annotated 'very_hard'/'extreme'), consistent with the intuition that dependency constraints increase ordering vulnerabilities. However, only five repairs were observed, limiting inference about repair efficacy across a broader range of failure modalities. Possible explanations consistent with archived evidence include (a) low prevalence of validator‑detectable violations in the sampled corpus, (b) generator behavior producing largely valid initial candidates for the declared model+prompt, and/or (c) validator coverage that omits some semantic error classes.

Design rationale, operational implications, and recommended follow‑ups. The shared_initial_candidate paired design intentionally isolates downstream validator and single‑repair effects and avoids conflation with prompt/decoding or sampling interventions. This yields a precise causal estimand (baseline initial validity versus final guarded validity after deterministic validation and up to one repair) but precludes measuring generator‑level interventions. Artifact‑grounded evidence shows that a deterministic validator plus a bounded single repair can avert some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflows; yet measurable marginal gains are small when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the repair budget is narrowly constrained. Supported, concrete follow‑ups include: (1) executing independent first‑pass generation arms to measure generator+validator interactions (preregistered but not run here under shared_initial_candidate); (2) sweeping repair budgets (0..k repairs) to quantify marginal returns per additional repair; (3) expanding validator rule suites and topology heterogeneity to probe external validity; and (4) evaluating multiple model families. Follow‑ups should prespecify baseline failure ranges and adjust power calculations to the expected operating regime.

Threats to validity. Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary reflects deterministic_netops_validator_v5 rule coverage; omitted policy checks would inflate measured success. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate downstream effects but prevent measuring first‑pass generation interventions. External validity: synthetic corpus and a single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) limit generalization to heterogeneous production environments. Conclusion validity: extreme baseline success produced sparse discordant counts and discrete p‑value behavior, reducing sensitivity for small absolute effects. These limitations were anticipated in the preregistration and are documented in the archived manifest.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1,000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar did not meet two‑sided α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total hosted model calls recorded = 1,005. The preregistered confirmatory result is the exact McNemar outcome; the paired bootstrap CI and one‑sided test are reported as descriptive and exploratory respectively. Artifact‑grounded evidence indicates downstream validator/repair safeguards can prevent some unsafe outcomes in structured NetOps workflows, but measurable marginal gains are constrained when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the paired design isolates downstream effects. Broader evaluations that vary generator semantics, repair budgets, validator coverage, and model families are needed to map marginal returns in realistic operating regimes.

Figure 2: Paired bootstrap distribution of the paired difference (guarded − baseline) from the preregistered executor (histogram with 95% percentile CI bounds). This visualization supplements the preregistered exact McNemar confirmatory test and illustrates bootstrap sensitivity to sparse discordant counts.

Orchestration and validator: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the validator/digital twin. Preregistration: study cand‑003‑stud‑001 (frozen prior to any model calls and recorded in the archived execution manifest). Immutable initial master prompt reference archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: after the autonomy lock the research run executed the preregistered experiment, analysis, and manuscript drafting; no human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
